what_it_does: RDNA 4 is AMD's latest graphics processor, an evolution of RDNA 3 aimed at both consumer gaming and professional computing workloads. It improves three core areas: the compute units (the chip's cores for doing math), the cache hierarchy (the pyramid of fast memory that sits between the processor and main memory), and the memory subsystem (how data flows in and out). The result is higher throughput—the ability to process more work per second—while drawing less power than previous generations.
